market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously bullish for today's session, driven almost entirely by diplomatic optimism around the UN General Assembly and hopes for a de-escalation in the Middle East that could bring oil prices sustainably lower. The key catalyst to watch is any concrete signal of progress on Iran diplomacy — Trump has indicated openness to meeting Iran's president at the General Assembly, and even a modest improvement in tensions could trigger an outsized oil selloff with significant positive knock-on macro effects. However, the underlying news flow remains net negative, so this rally could fade quickly if diplomacy disappoints.

On the trade front, the US-China truce extension was not reached on Sunday, and Washington is expected to hike aggregate tariff rates on Chinese imports back to pre-SCOTUS IEEPA levels in the coming weeks, creating a fresh macro headwind.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's your Monday September 21st morning game plan.

The macro setup this morning is genuinely confusing — futures are rallying solidly with the S&P up about 49 points, the Nasdaq up 329, and the Russell up 13 and a half points, even though nearly everything that hit the tape over the weekend was negative. Asia closed broadly higher, Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points, and Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points. The one thing holding this rally together is diplomatic optimism heading into the United Nations General Assembly in New York, which runs through September 28th. Trump signaled over the weekend that he would be open to meeting Iran's president at the event, and he reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. The bull thesis here is straightforward — nearly every macro problem markets face right now traces back to oil. If diplomacy produces even a modest de-escalation, energy prices drop hard, and that unlocks lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, and improved consumer confidence. Brent is already sliding about 170 basis points this morning to around 102 dollars.

On the Fed side, policy remains hawkish globally. The market is pricing roughly 33 basis points of additional rate hikes across the final two Fed meetings this year, with about 50/50 odds on an October 28th move. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both made hawkish remarks late last week, warning that inflation is running hot well beyond just energy. Treasury is also planning to flood the market with over a trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above 24 percent of marketable debt — well above their own 20 percent target.

On the company side, Novo Nordisk is the biggest mover to flag — shares are falling in Europe after the company disappointed investors at its analyst day by failing to provide granular financial targets, despite touting future pipeline launches. Oracle remains under pressure following a negative piece about financing troubles tied to its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, where efforts to offload loans have reportedly hit a wall. Those Oracle headlines are part of a broader wave of ugly AI infrastructure news from the weekend — OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars through 2030, Anthropic's IPO is delayed, and Anthropic's 2027 annual recurring revenue projections reportedly underwhelmed. Despite all of that, data center pick-and-shovel names are actually holding up in Europe this morning, which is notable. On the positive side, Disney's parks business is outperforming peers by leaning into price promotions and package deals. And the Paramount-Warner deal continues to inch toward a potential California settlement that could include CNN independence protections and cable channel divestitures.

The week's major catalysts beyond today include US flash PMIs Wednesday morning, the Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, and most importantly the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday, which could produce modest tariff reductions on roughly 30 billion dollars of goods. There are no major earnings today.

Bottom line: the rally is real but fragile. It's built entirely on hope that the UN General Assembly produces something tangible on Middle East diplomacy. If it doesn't, the negative weekend news flow will reassert itself quickly. Trade cautiously and keep your eyes on any Iran headline.
